description: "Vectors, linear constraints, matrices, bases, rank and projections applied to one dataset."

## Why machine learning needs linear algebra

Our six invented delivery orders contain two measured features. The model stores them as a matrix and uses one parameter vector for all rows. This turns many individual arithmetic expressions into one linear-algebra operation.

$$
X=\begin{bmatrix}
1&1&1\\
1&2&2\\
1&3&1\\
1&4&3\\
1&5&2\\
1&6&3
\end{bmatrix},\quad
\boldsymbol\beta=
\begin{bmatrix}\beta_0\\\beta_1\\\beta_2\end{bmatrix},\quad
\hat{\boldsymbol y}=X\boldsymbol\beta.
$$

The first column is the intercept, the second is distance and the third is the number of items. The shape contract is $X\in\mathbb R^{6\times3}$ and $\beta\in\mathbb R^3$. **It is mathematically invalid to multiply incompatible shapes.**

## Three mathematical questions

**Existence:** Does a system $A\boldsymbol x=\boldsymbol b$ have any exact solution? If not, least squares estimates a useful approximate answer.

**Identifiability:** Are columns of $X$ linearly independent? If we add a column equal to distance+items, it is redundant and the parameter vector may cease to be unique.

**Geometry:** What part of observed $\boldsymbol y$ can the model represent? Orthogonal projection separates fitted predictions from residuals:

$$
X^\top(\boldsymbol y-X\hat\beta)=0.
$$

This says the residual is orthogonal to each feature column at a least-squares optimum. It is a deeper explanation of regression than 'fit a straight line'.

### Calculate for yourself

Take $\beta=(3,2,2)^\top$. The prediction for the first order is 7 minutes, and the second is 11 minutes versus an observed 12. Compute the remaining predictions and total squared error before checking them with Python.

~~~bash
python3 ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py linear
python3 ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py geometry
~~~

**Further connections:** [PCA](chapters/10-principal-component-analysis/index.qmd) is an application of eigendecomposition and orthogonal projection. [Regression](chapters/09-linear-regression/index.qmd) uses rank, projection and numerical solution.
